note: Conformance vectors for the node tree's rules: the order a level lists its nodes in (`order`: folders first, then every other node mixed by name, case and accents aside, digits as numbers, equal names by creation then id), the numbering of siblings that carry one name (`displayNames`), whether a name collides with a sibling's (`collision`, over the kinds' token inputs, ADR 0080 decision 16), and the move's plan (`moveBlock`, `moveBlockOf`, `planMove`, `movePlaces`, `moveTrail`, `moveStart`; ADR 0080 decision 11 for identity folders). Each case names the rule it pins (`rule`). Inputs chosen by hand; every `expected` recorded by running the rules and read against its rule before commit. A tree (`trees`) is the nodes a session reads, `rootId` its top (null: a member's scope root); a mode `guest` places only into a folder. `kinds` is the kind table both clients read (the web's registry, the apps' AppKinds). `order` was first read from Intl.Collator(locale, { numeric: true, sensitivity: 'base' }) in English and in German, which agree on every case (`icu`). The shape: v1-vectors.schema.json.

order.rule: folders first, then every other node mixed by name, not grouped by kind
a folder named Zzz before a file named Aaa: the kind decides first
digits read as numbers, leading zeros aside: Foto 2 before Foto 10, Foto 02 ties with Foto 2 (the older first)
case and accents aside: a, A and Ä are one letter; equal names tie by creation
a sharp s is ss, the capital sharp s too
a name led by white space, punctuation or a symbol sorts before digits and letters, in the collator's order of the groups
punctuation and symbols outside ASCII take their place in the same groups
an emoji is a symbol: after the punctuation, before the currency signs, digits and letters
other scripts after Latin: Greek, Cyrillic, then the CJK ideographs
names that fold to nothing for a slug still order: the empty name first
ligatures and letters the collator reads as their base letters: æ is ae, ø is o, ł is l, a full-width letter is the letter
white space inside a name is one of its characters, before punctuation and letters: a tab before a space, a no-break space is a space
equal names tie by creation, then by id in UTF-16 order (B before a), whatever order the tree listed them in
a guest's nodes carry no creation instant (null): equal names tie by id
folders and others are ordered apart, each by the same rule

displayNames.rule: a unique name keeps itself; a repeated one is numbered from (2) in creation order (the instant, then the id)
a guest's view numbers in node-id order (no creation instant is served)
the numbering compares names exactly: case and accents tell names apart
two born in one millisecond fall to their ids in UTF-16 order (B before a)
display only: a sibling literally named Anna (2) and the second Anna read alike
